key_insight: SegviGen repurposes pretrained 3D generative models as structured priors to produce accurate 3D part segmentation, avoiding heavy annotation or multi-view aggregation and reducing cross-view inconsistency.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between costly, annotation-heavy native 3D discriminative segmentation and inconsistent 2D-to-3D distillation approaches by enabling reliable part segmentation using existing pretrained 3D generative models.
method: Extract and leverage structured spatial/latent priors encoded in a pretrained 3D generative model to inform part label prediction.
Train a lightweight segmentation head or mapping that converts generative features/representation into part labels with minimal additional supervision.
Apply consistency and boundary-aware refinement to produce sharp, cross-view-consistent part boundaries without extensive 3D annotations.
impact: SegviGen lowers the annotation and compute barrier for high-quality 3D part segmentation, enabling practitioners to reuse generative models for downstream segmentation tasks and improving robustness of 3D pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pretrained 3D generative model -> feature/latent extraction -> lightweight segmentation head -> refined part-labeled 3D output.
Before/after comparison: multi-view aggregated masks (blurry, inconsistent) vs SegviGen outputs (crisp, consistent part boundaries).
Color-coded 3D model gallery showing segmented parts across object categories to illustrate generalization.
Bar chart or infographic comparing annotation cost and segmentation accuracy for distillation, native discriminative training, and SegviGen.
paper_title: SegviGen: Repurposing 3D Generative Model for Part Segmentation
paper_authors: Lin Li, Haoran Feng, Zehuan Huang, Haohua Chen, Wenbo Nie
